Resistors in Series and Parallel; the E24 Series

findings.notes: All 24 values match IEC 60063 E24 preferred-number series exactly.

findings.claim: Resistor colour code: Black=0, Brown=1, Red=2, Orange=3, Yellow=4, Green=5, Blue=6, Violet=7, Grey=8, White=9; Gold=×0.1, Silver=×0.01; gold band 4 = ±5%, silver = ±10%, none = ±20%
findings.notes: All digit assignments, multiplier exceptions, and tolerance values match IEC 60062 standard.

lesson_title: Sensing Circuits and Voltage Dividers

findings.claim: Red LED forward voltage approximately 2V; blue or white LED approximately 3V
findings.notes: Red LEDs: typical range 1.6–2.2V, so ~2V is a reasonable central value. Blue/white LEDs: typical range is 3.0–3.6V; quoting '3V' is at the bottom of the range. At GCSE level this is the conventional teaching approximation and matches Eduqas exam data sheet values, but students should be aware the actual value can be higher. Not a factual error for GCSE purposes.

lesson_title: Transistor and MOSFET Switching Circuits

findings.claim: npn transistor base-emitter voltage V_BE ≈ 0.7 V when on
findings.notes: Standard silicon BJT V_BE ≈ 0.6–0.7V. Using 0.7V as the GCSE design value is the universally accepted approximation.

lesson_title: Voltage Comparators
Diodes, Half-Wave Rectification and Zener Voltage Regulation

findings.claim: Silicon diode forward voltage drop approximately 0.7 V; this value stays nearly constant over a wide range of currents
findings.notes: Standard silicon diode V_F = 0.6–0.8V; 0.7V is the accepted teaching approximation and is broadly constant across typical operating currents.

lesson_title: Logic Gates, Truth Tables and Boolean Algebra

findings.claim: Boolean algebra is 'a branch of mathematics developed by George Boole that uses only 0s and 1s'
findings.notes: George Boole (1815–1864) developed Boolean algebra; his 1847 work 'The Mathematical Analysis of Logic' and 1854 'An Investigation of the Laws of Thought' established the foundation. The characterisation as using only 0s and 1s is correct for digital applications.

findings.claim: NAND gate is a universal gate because any logic function can be built from NAND gates alone
findings.notes: Functional completeness of NAND is a standard result in digital logic.

lesson_title: Designing Logic Systems and NAND-Only Implementations

findings.claim: The 4011 contains four two-input NAND gates; the 4001 contains four two-input NOR gates
findings.notes: CD4011 = quad 2-input NAND in 14-pin DIP; CD4001 = quad 2-input NOR in 14-pin DIP. Both confirmed from datasheets.

findings.claim: 14-pin DIL package, pin 14 is V_DD (supply), pin 7 is V_SS (ground) for the 4011
findings.notes: Standard pinout for CD4011: pin 14 = VDD, pin 7 = VSS. Confirmed from multiple datasheets.

findings.claim: Pins are numbered anticlockwise from pin 1 (top left when notch faces up)
findings.notes: Standard DIP package pin numbering: counterclockwise from pin 1 at top-left (with notch at top). This is the universal convention for through-hole DIP ICs.

lesson_title: Amplifiers: Gain, Bandwidth and Clipping

findings.claim: Bandwidth is defined between the two frequencies at which gain drops to 70% of its maximum value (the half-power points or −3 dB points)
findings.notes: The −3 dB point corresponds to 0.707 (≈70%) of the maximum voltage gain, which is the half-power point. This is the standard engineering definition of bandwidth.

findings.claim: Audio amplifiers need a bandwidth covering at least 20 Hz to 20 kHz to reproduce the full range of human hearing
findings.notes: Standard accepted range of human hearing is 20 Hz–20 kHz.

lesson_title: Inverting and Non-Inverting Op-Amp Circuits
Summing Amplifiers and Audio Mixer Systems
RC Time Delays and the 555 Monostable

findings.claim: 555 monostable pulse duration: T = 1.1 × R × C; the 1.1 factor reflects the capacitor charging to two-thirds of the supply voltage before the output resets
findings.notes: The standard monostable formula T = 1.1RC is derived from the 2/3 Vcc threshold. Confirmed from Texas Instruments LM555 datasheet and multiple authoritative sources.

findings.claim: Trigger on pin 2 below one-third of supply voltage starts monostable cycle
findings.notes: Pin 2 triggers when pulled below 1/3 Vcc. This is the lower comparator threshold. Confirmed.

findings.claim: 555 timer output can source or sink up to 200 mA to drive LEDs, relays or other loads directly without additional transistor stages
findings.notes: The LM555 datasheet specifies 200 mA maximum output current (source or sink). The claim that this removes the need for a transistor driver for small loads is accurate at this current level.

findings.claim: 555 contains an internal comparator, a bistable latch, a discharge transistor, and a voltage divider — all inside a single 8-pin IC
findings.notes: The 555 timer is indeed an 8-pin IC containing two comparators, a voltage divider (three 5kΩ resistors), an SR flip-flop (bistable latch), and an NPN discharge transistor on pin 7.

lesson_title: 555 Astable Oscillators and Mark-Space Ratio

findings.claim: 555 astable frequency: f = 1.44 / ((R1 + 2R2) × C); T_ON = 0.7 × (R1 + R2) × C; T_OFF = 0.7 × R2 × C
findings.notes: All three formulae are standard for the 555 astable configuration. Confirmed from multiple datasheets and electronics references. The 1.44 factor comes from 1/ln(2) × 1 ≈ 1.443 (from RC charging equations to 2/3 and 1/3 Vcc thresholds).

findings.claim: Mark-space ratio = (R1 + R2) / R2; standard 555 astable cannot achieve exactly 50% duty cycle unless R1 = 0 Ω
findings.notes: Because T_ON includes charging through both R1 and R2, the mark time is always greater than the space time when R1 > 0, so the duty cycle always exceeds 50%. A diode-modified circuit is the standard fix.

lesson_title: D-Type Flip-Flops, Latches and Up-Counters

findings.claim: D-type flip-flop is rising-edge triggered: Q copies D only at the rising clock edge; holds value between edges
findings.notes: Rising-edge-triggered D-type flip-flop is standard. The symbol uses a small triangle on the clock input to indicate edge-triggering. Correct.

lesson_title: Binary, BCD and Decade Counters with 7-Segment Displays

findings.claim: The 4017 Johnson counter IC produces ten sequential HIGH outputs (Q0 to Q9) in order; pin 15 (MR, master reset) can reset the counter
findings.notes: CD4017 is a 16-pin IC with 10 decoded outputs (Q0–Q9) stepping sequentially on each rising clock edge. Pin 15 is the master reset (MR), active HIGH. Confirmed from datasheet.

findings.claim: 7-segment display digit segment patterns for 0–9 (a–g encoding table)
findings.notes: All 10 digit patterns in the table match the standard 7-segment encoding as documented in Wikipedia's seven-segment display character representations article.

findings.claim: For a 4017 with output Q_N wired to MR, the modulo is N (the counter visits states 0 through N−1)
findings.notes: When Q_N goes HIGH it immediately fires the reset, so Q_N is only a glitch. The counter counts N stable states (0 to N−1). Confirmed from manufacturer reference and electronics-tutorials.

lesson_title: Schmitt Inverters and Interfacing Analogue to Digital
Microcontrollers and Flowchart Programming

findings.claim: PIC stands for Peripheral Interface Controller
findings.notes: PIC historically stood for Peripheral Interface Controller (the original design by General Instrument was a peripheral controller for the CP1600). Microchip no longer uses it as an acronym, but the expansion 'Peripheral Interface Controller' is the historically accurate one.

lesson_title: Microcontroller Applications and System Evaluation

findings.claim: ABS pulses the brake hydraulics at around 15 times per second
findings.notes: ABS modulation frequency is typically 5–15 Hz depending on the system. '15 times per second' is the upper bound of the commonly cited range and is consistent with published sources.

findings.claim: Airbag deployment: entire sequence from impact to full inflation takes around 30 milliseconds
findings.notes: Front airbags are fully inflated within approximately 20–30 ms from crash onset. '~30 ms' is within the published range.
